answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive by requiring each newcomer to lock a bond before entering a task market. Existing agents randomly audit its signed work through a prism of independent checks; consistent answers build reputation and unlock larger jobs, while a proven lie burns the bond and reduces future selection. A sybil attacker must fund many deposits and coordinate them across each inlet and reef, yet one detected collusion can slash linked accounts, making fake identities costlier than honest participation.
